purpose: Reusable answer-quality rules for turning deterministic groundwater metrics into useful interpretation.

cohort_meaning.goal: Explain the value and limits of a cohort average for monitored wells.
required_moves: Define the cohort average as a group summary, not a physical well.
Explain whether the group-level signal is broadly falling, rising, or near stable.
Warn that the average can hide divergent individual wells.
Use fastest-declining and strongest-rising wells to show why outliers matter.
Frame screening risk as a prioritization flag, not a forecast.
Tell the reader what to check next.
weak_answer_signals: Only lists rates or site IDs.
Treats the average as if every well behaves the same way.
Does not explain why highlighted or divergent wells matter.
Does not separate observed data from interpretation.
cohort_meaning.student_takeaway: Start with the cohort average to understand the group, then inspect individual wells to see whether the average is hiding stress, recovery, or divergence.

decline_explanation.goal: Explain a falling groundwater signal without overclaiming causation.
required_moves: State the observed decline from deterministic metrics.
Explain that decline can suggest drawdown or reduced aquifer pressure.
Refuse to prove pumping or recharge change from the chart alone.
Name external evidence needed to test causes.
Explain why the pattern matters for monitoring or sustainability.
weak_answer_signals: Only repeats the annual rate.
Claims a cause without pumping, rainfall, recharge, or model evidence.
Leaves out caveats.
decline_explanation.student_takeaway: A declining line is an observation; drawdown, pumping stress, recharge change, and saltwater concern are hypotheses that need more evidence.

shallow_deep_comparison.goal: Compare aquifer-depth groups while respecting proxy limits.
required_moves: Compare group mean rates directly.
Explain why shallow and deep/confined wells can behave differently.
Mention seasonal variability when available.
Warn that depth alone does not prove hydraulic connection.
Identify what construction or screened-interval evidence would confirm the comparison.
weak_answer_signals: Dumps well metadata without saying whether the groups diverge.
Assumes shallow/deep wells represent the same aquifer behavior.
Ignores seasonal or confinement context.
shallow_deep_comparison.student_takeaway: Compare the groups first, then ask whether aquifer setting, screened interval, and seasonality make them fair proxies for each other.

fastest_changing.goal: Identify the most rapidly changing well and contextualize it within the cohort.
required_moves: Name the fastest-changing well and its annual rate.
Compare it to the next most negative or strongest rising well.
Relate it to the cohort mean to show whether it is an outlier or representative.
Explain what 'fastest' means for monitoring priority, not for proving a cause.
weak_answer_signals: Only lists rates without interpreting what they mean.
Does not compare to any other well or the cohort.
Claims a cause for the fast change without evidence.
fastest_changing.student_takeaway: The fastest-changing well tells you where to focus investigation, not what is causing the change.

risk_explanation.goal: Explain cohort screening risk as a triage flag, not a diagnosis.
required_moves: Quantify the percentage of wells falling.
Name the strongest contributor to the risk level.
Explain that screening risk prioritizes follow-up, it does not prove harm.
Suggest what additional evidence would clarify the risk.
weak_answer_signals: Treats risk level as a definitive assessment rather than a screening flag.
Does not name specific wells contributing to the risk.
Omits caveats about what the risk level cannot tell you.
risk_explanation.student_takeaway: Screening risk is a prioritization tool: it tells you which cohorts deserve follow-up, not which are in danger.

trend_change.goal: Explain detected changepoints as observed pattern shifts, not proven causes.
required_moves: Name the well and approximate date of the trend shift.
Compare pre-shift and post-shift annual rates.
Explain that a changepoint is a statistical detection, not proof of a specific event.
Note what outside data (land-use change, policy, drought) would confirm the timing.
weak_answer_signals: Claims a specific cause for the trend shift without evidence.
Only mentions the changepoint date without comparing rates.
Does not explain what a changepoint detection means statistically.
trend_change.student_takeaway: A trend shift tells you when the pattern changed, but proving why requires overlaying outside data like pumping records or rainfall.

seasonal.goal: Explain seasonal patterns and their relationship to long-term trends.
required_moves: Compare wet-season and dry-season averages.
Report the seasonal amplitude and whether it varies across wells.
Explain whether per-season trends are worsening, recovering, or stable.
Warn that large seasonal swings can mask or mimic long-term trends.
weak_answer_signals: Only reports seasonal means without discussing their significance.
Does not mention the risk of confusing seasonal variation with long-term decline.
Ignores per-season trend directions.
seasonal.student_takeaway: Separate the seasonal cycle from the multi-year signal before drawing conclusions about long-term change.

cause_or_why.goal: Distinguish observed signals from unproven causal claims.
required_moves: State the observed signal clearly from deterministic metrics.
List plausible explanations as hypotheses, not conclusions.
Name the external evidence needed to test each hypothesis.
Explicitly refuse to confirm causation from the chart alone.
weak_answer_signals: Claims a cause without mentioning evidence requirements.
Skips the observation step and jumps to speculation.
Does not name specific external data sources needed.
cause_or_why.student_takeaway: The chart shows the pattern; proving the cause requires pumping records, rainfall data, recharge models, or water-quality evidence.

general.goal: Provide a grounded interpretation that connects observed data to aquifer context.
required_moves: State the observed signal from chart metrics.
Connect it to the relevant hydrogeologic setting.
Mention any notable patterns (changepoints, divergent pairs, seasonal swings) if present.
State what the chart cannot tell you.
weak_answer_signals: Returns a single generic sentence without referencing specific data.
Does not connect the signal to aquifer context.
Omits caveats about the limits of the available data.
general.student_takeaway: Start with what the data shows, connect it to the aquifer setting, then note what additional evidence would strengthen the interpretation.
